# Le Tsuan Design — Full Project Case Studies

> Complete technical write-ups for every project in the portfolio. Each entry includes client, location, year, category, area (when available), and the full design and engineering narrative. Sourced from the live project pages on letsuan.com.

## How to use this file
- For a quick studio overview and curated links, see /llms.txt
- High-priority case studies (major museum exhibitions, international work, complex engineering, licensed IP) appear first
- Each project follows a consistent structure for easier parsing

## Studio Snapshot
- Founded: 2014
- Studios: Taichung and Taipei, Taiwan
- Delivery model: Design-build — the same team carries projects from concept through fabrication and on-site installation
- Projects delivered: 42+
- Space completed: 17,000+ m²
- Primary clients: National Museum of Natural Science, National Museum of History, National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts, Ministry of Culture, R.O.C. Air Force Academy, Ørsted, TSMC, HTC VIVE Arts, Toei Animation, Shogakukan, Mizuki Production

## Core Technical Competencies & Specializations
- **Zero-Penetration & Heritage Building Construction**: Free-standing structural frameworks, tensioned mounting, and counterweight systems that comply with strict non-drilling preservation rules (Huashan 1914, Songshan Cultural Park, Pier-2, National Museum of History, Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall).
- **High-Density AV & Interactive Integration**: Node-by-node load calculations for large projector arrays (170+ units), free-roaming VR charging infrastructure (100+ headsets), motion sensors, pneumatic/IR triggers, DMX lighting choreography, and automated kinetic installations.
- **Museum-Grade Conservation Engineering**: Constant-humidity micro-environment display cases, optical-fiber / low-lux preservation lighting (50–150 lux), airtight case sealing, Class-1 fire-retardant material fabrication.
- **Harsh Environment & Coastal Engineering**: Anti-corrosion fluorocarbon coatings, 304 stainless steel structures, salt-tolerant coastal landscape planning, and installations designed for high UV and wind exposure.
- **Design-Build Delivery**: Single team responsible for curatorial concept, spatial design, fabrication, MEP coordination, and on-site installation under compressed schedules and complex constraints.

## Seeing is Believing? — Masters of Marine Illusion: Mimicry & Camouflage

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-marine-illusion  
**Client:** Taichung Aquarium  
**Location:** Taichung, Taiwan  
**Year:** 2026  
**Area:** 68 ㎡  
**Category:** Exhibition Design, Graphic Design, Visual Design, Installation Art, Construction

### Summary
Full design-build for Taichung Aquarium’s marine mimicry and camouflage exhibition. Within a tightly constrained 68 m² footprint, the team solved visitor circulation, living-specimen lighting requirements, fully concealed MEP, and used eco-certified materials throughout.

### Challenge
The exhibition space measured only 68 square meters. Fitting a coherent story about seven species (including the mimic octopus and pharaoh cuttlefish) while protecting live animals and maintaining clear circulation was the primary constraint.

### Approach
Ultra-thin wall linings recovered floor area for circulation and a central motion-sensing interactive zone. Aquarium tanks were arranged in a stepped, cascading layout that served both adult and child sightlines. All wiring for life-support, lighting, and sensors was embedded inside the thin wall assembly. Screens, speakers, and projectors were recessed flush. Power for life support ran on a separate circuit from interactive and AV systems.

### Materials and Lighting
Wall substrates, coatings, trim, and full-space graphics carried international environmental certifications, including the Green Building Material Label. Graphics used eco-certified non-woven fabric (recycled fiber, Class 1 fire retardancy, formaldehyde-free). Lighting used a deep-sea blue base (#00183A) with selective fluorescent cyan and warning-yellow accents, keeping ambient levels low enough not to stress the living specimens.

---

## Eternal Notre-Dame — International Debut of the VR Immersive Exhibition in Taiwan

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-notre-dame  
**Client:** HTC / National Science and Technology Museum  
**Location:** Kaohsiung, Taiwan  
**Year:** 2023–2024  
**Area:** 720.64 ㎡  
**Category:** Exhibition Design, Installation Art, Interactive Multimedia, Construction

### Summary
Taiwan debut of the Eternal Notre-Dame free-roaming VR exhibition. Le Tsuan handled spatial planning, construction drawings, wall-graphic production, and full on-site build across 720.64 m² in 12 days under strict non-drilling rules and a 5% maximum light-level variance required by the French technical team.

### Key Constraints
- No drilling or fastening into existing walls or structure
- Lighting variance across the entire venue held under 5%
- Over 100 simultaneous VR devices with rotational charging
- Shared elevator for material transport; construction coincided with Typhoon Khanun
- Seismic considerations for all freestanding and suspended elements

### Approach
Non-destructive freestanding and support-based construction completed light-blocking, partitions, and equipment supports without damaging the building. Lighting fixtures on 10-meter steel beams were suspended rather than fastened, protecting fireproof foam. Approximately 500 meters of curved-facade graphics were produced and installed with continuous alignment. Electrical load was calculated for more than 100 wearable VR sets. All structural elements were evaluated for seismic safety factors.

### Outcome
The exhibition met the international technical team’s specifications, passed venue and fire-department inspections, and opened successfully as the first stop of the Asia tour.

---

## Beyond Just an Exhibition — You Are Part of the Art! (teamLab)

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-beyond-just-an-exhibition  
**Client:** teamLab  
**Location:** National Taiwan Science Education Center, Taipei  
**Year:** 2024  
**Area:** 1,859.126 ㎡  
**Category:** Exhibition Design, Installation Art, Event

### Summary
Full spatial planning, construction drawings, and general contracting for teamLab Future Park Taipei. A 1,859 m² floor was fitted with 178 projectors plus blending processors, sensors, and terminals in 14 days. The team remained on site through the full run and completed teardown and clearance within seven days of closing.

### Key Engineering Challenges
- Projectors, speakers, and sensors suspended from truss below the 8th-floor slab; load distribution calculated node by node
- Raised access flooring up to 2.5 m high required structural reinforcement while allowing cable routing
- Walls could not be drilled; partitions used structural tie-in methods
- Full blackout required against curved glass walls and adjacent bright spaces
- Power system reconfigured for the high simultaneous load

### Operational Issues Resolved During Run
Projected-image drift was traced (via displacement and gyroscopic sensors) to air-conditioning airflow vibrating the projectors; ductwork was re-wrapped and redirected without reducing visitor comfort. HDMI chip failures caused by bundled signal/power cables and static were resolved with proper separation and insulating mats. A slide landing angle was retrofitted after visitor reports.

### Outcome
The exhibition operated successfully through its run. Full dismantling and site restoration were completed within the required seven-day window.

---

## Detention — Reality Experience

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-detention-pier2  
**Location:** Songshan Cultural and Creative Park, Taipei / The Pier-2 Art Center, Kaohsiung  
**Year:** 2020–2021  
**Area:** Songshan 1,210 ㎡ / Pier-2 1,190.2 ㎡  
**Category:** Exhibition Design, Interior Design, Graphic Design, Visual Design, Construction

### Summary
Immersive adaptation of the acclaimed Taiwanese horror game Detention. A multi-layered physical experience was built across two venues, recreating a 1960s Taiwanese high school with period-accurate aging, scent, sound, and triggered mechanisms while fully satisfying fire-code and evacuation requirements.

### Core Contradiction Solved
The game demanded extremely low light, maze-like enclosure, and extensive aged timber. Fire code demanded high-visibility exit signage, wide accessible routes, and Class-1 fire-retardant materials. Four invisible-design techniques resolved the conflict: smart DMX-controlled evacuation lighting that stayed minimal until emergency, nano fire-retardant impregnation of all wood and fabric, staggered walls that preserved visual tightness while maintaining 1.2–1.5 m clear width, and ultra-low-power baseboard LED strips that did not break dark adaptation.

### Experience Design
Genuine 1960s campus objects were collected or custom-fabricated and professionally aged. Directional 3D sound, precision scent diffusion, pneumatic and infrared triggers, water-mist rain effects, and UV-reactive hidden messages were choreographed with NPC actor ambush points.

### Outcome
A frightening dark exhibit and a code-compliant public venue were delivered as a single integrated system across two cities.

---

## Detective Conan — Science Investigation Exhibition (Taipei & Kaohsiung)

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-detective-conan-taipei  
**Client:** Shogakukan Inc.  
**Location:** National Taiwan Science Education Center, Taipei / National Science and Technology Museum, Kaohsiung  
**Year:** 2019–2020  
**Category:** Exhibition Design, Interior Design, Graphic Design, Visual Design, Construction

### Summary
Licensed Detective Conan forensic-science exhibition adapted for two Taiwanese venues of different scales. The team handled circulation planning, set reconstruction matched to original anime/manga references, interactive forensic devices, crowd-flow engineering, and post-show teardown with component reuse between cities.

### Approach
Two staggered circulation tracks (hardcore forensics vs. lighter deduction) naturally split crowds. Sets for the crime scene, Mouri Detective Agency, and Poirot Cafe were cross-checked against source material for proportions, furniture, typography, and color. Queue and bottleneck points were pre-mapped; dual-route booklets, multi-station forensic devices, calculated corridor widths, and real-time wait displays managed peak summer traffic.

### Outcome
Consistent IP fidelity was maintained across two buildings. Reusable components from the Taipei run were refurbished for Kaohsiung, avoiding full recalculation.

---

## Experience the Yokai World — 100 Stories of Yokai Exhibition

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-yokai-world  
**Client:** Mizuki Production  
**Location:** Huashan Creative Park, Taipei  
**Year:** 2022–2023  
**Area:** 958.68 ㎡  
**Category:** Exhibition Design, Construction

### Summary
Centennial exhibition for Mizuki Shigeru, first stop outside Japan. A fully immersive dark-exhibit environment of 958.68 ㎡ was built under strict zero-penetration heritage rules and a compressed pandemic-era schedule, then passed Mizuki Production’s on-site inspection in a single round.

### Key Constraints
- No drilling or structural contact with the heritage building
- High-density FRP sculptural sets, multi-zone automated triggers, full audio-lighting-electrical integration
- Absolute blackout required before any other system could function
- Tens of thousands of daily trigger cycles demanded industrial-grade durability

### Approach
Self-supporting steel-and-timber frame with modular raised floor transferred all load independently. Sensors (PIR, microwave, pressure) were fully concealed. Wiring and pneumatics ran inside set maintenance corridors. 24-hour phased construction by trade kept headcount compliant with pandemic rules.

### Outcome
Zero system failures across the run. Licensor inspection passed on the first attempt with no resubmissions.

---

## Universe — 500 Pieces of LED Kinetic Light

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-led-kinetic  
**Client:** Grandview Mall Science Museum  
**Location:** Canton (Guangzhou), China  
**Year:** 2024  
**Category:** Exhibition Design, Installation Art, Interactive Multimedia, Construction

### Summary
Design and technical planning for a large-scale kinetic lighting installation of 500 independently winched LED fixtures, controlled by a single software system. The work functions as both functional illumination and the primary visual centerpiece of the science museum space, synchronized with music and narration to convey astronomical concepts.

### Technical Planning
Each fixture’s vertical position is controlled by its own winch; RGB LED modules handle color and brightness. All motion and lighting parameters are unified under specialized control software. Synchronization logic between winch motion paths and color transitions was developed so the array can form varied, layered spatial compositions rather than simple up-and-down movement, producing fine detail and dynamic tension.

---

## Cat Art Museum — A Super-Healing World by Shu Yamamoto

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-cat-art  
**Client:** Cat Art Museum  
**Location:** Pingtung 1936 Tobacco Culture Base, Taiwan  
**Year:** 2024  
**Category:** Exhibition Design, Graphic Design, Visual Design, Installation Art, Construction

### Summary
Spatial design that translates Japanese artist Shu Yamamoto’s cat-themed paintings into three-dimensional immersive environments. Large saturated color zones, true-scale character figures, extended mural-and-furniture scenes, and continuous photo-point planning turned the visit into an active experience rather than passive viewing.

### Approach
Instead of a neutral white-box gallery, the space was divided into sequential saturated color zones (olive, caramel, lavender, magenta, indigo). Selected characters were reproduced at true scale with dedicated lighting and backdrops. Perspective-matched murals and physical props allowed visitors to sit inside the scenes. Every residual corner was pre-designed as a photo point.

---

## La Fortuna Bordada — Taiwanese Embroidery in Madrid

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-la-fortuna-bordada  
**Client:** National Museum of History  
**Location:** Museo Nacional de Artes Decorativas, Madrid, Spain  
**Year:** 2017  
**Category:** Exhibition Design, Interior Design, Graphic Design, Visual Design, Logo Design

### Summary
Spatial planning and exhibition construction design for the first full presentation of Taiwanese embroidery within Spain’s national museum system. The entire project was delivered remotely: complete construction drawings were produced in Taiwan and executed by a local Spanish contractor. No Le Tsuan personnel were on site in Madrid.

### Approach
Dedicated case structures and garment-suspension systems were designed around the fragility and light sensitivity of embroidered artifacts. Custom acrylic stands were created for three-dimensional accessories. Key visuals translated auspicious embroidery motifs into a visual system readable by Western audiences. Drawings had to be fully self-explanatory because no on-site adjustment was possible.

### Outcome
All 74 groups of artifacts were installed with correct dimensions and presentation through a single complete set of construction documents.

## The Missing Scientist — Electromagnetic Horizon II

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-missing-scientist  
**Client:** National Museum of Natural Science  
**Location:** Chelungpu Fault Preservation Park, Nantou, Taiwan  
**Year:** 2023–Present  
**Category:** Curatorial Project, Exhibition Design, Graphic Design, Visual Design, Interactive Multimedia, Construction

### Summary
Major update of a permanent electromagnetic-physics exhibition hall. Most existing structure and circulation were retained under budget constraints; selected interactive pieces were re-skinned and re-narrated, while new installations (including a motorized waveform theater) were added. Work proceeded under pandemic personnel limits and involved 12 specialist partners.

### Notable Installation
The Wave Dance Theater suspends dozens of independently motorized spheres that trace transverse and longitudinal waves in real time, with integrated AR identification. Ceiling structure was reinforced and a new truss system installed to carry the load.

## See the Ministry of Culture — One History. Six Departments. Countless Everyday Moments.

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-art-gallery-culture  
**Client:** Ministry of Culture  
**Year:** 2019  
**Category:** Curation, Exhibition Design, Graphic Design, Interactive Multimedia, Construction

### Summary
Curatorial concept treating the Ministry’s history and current structure as a packaging die-line that visitors “unwrap.” The entire exhibition was executed as non-fixed, freestanding construction to avoid triggering interior-alteration review of the building’s occupancy permit. Six departmental multimedia stations provide layered policy information; an exit interactive collects public input.

## Green Energy Education Observation Platform

**Source:** https://letsuan.com/project-tccge-deck

**Year:** 2022–Present
